sections.h2: Can I sell my house fast in Texarkana, TX?
sections.html:
Yes. Texarkana owners can list with an agent, sell to a cash buyer, or negotiate a quick as-is sale, and the right choice turns on how soon you must close and how much work the house needs.

One detail is specific to this city: Texarkana is split by the Texas-Arkansas line into two separate municipalities. A house on the Texas side, in Bowie County, falls under Texas property law, Texas tax rules and Bowie County records. If your address is on the Arkansas side, different state rules apply, so confirm which side of State Line Avenue the property sits on before you read anything else.

  • Open-market listing: widest audience, slowest and least predictable.
  • Cash purchase: the buyer pays without a mortgage and can often close in a few weeks.
  • Pre-sale tax and lien cleanup: worth doing first if you suspect back taxes.

sections.h2: What makes Texarkana, Texas different from other Texas cities?
sections.html:
It is a twin city. The Handbook of Texas says the name joins Texas, Arkansas and Louisiana, that State Line Avenue was laid out along the state border, and that the two sides keep their own mayors, councils and city officials while sharing some services such as fire protection and sewage disposal.

The Texas side was platted by the Texas and Pacific Railway after the town was established on December 8, 1873. The Handbook describes Texarkana as the junction of Interstate 30 and U.S. highways 59, 67, 71 and 82, and as the medical, educational and commercial center for a wider area that reaches into Oklahoma and Louisiana. It names Texarkana College and three major hospitals, and says the Red River Army Depot and Lone Star Army Ammunition plant helped the local economy recover in the early 1940s.

Wright Patman Lake and the Millwood Reservoir are noted as water supplies and recreation sites. For sellers, the practical point is a market built on health care, education and industry, plus a buyer pool that includes people from both sides of the line.

sections.h2: How do Bowie County property taxes work for a Texarkana seller?
sections.html:
Bowie Central Appraisal District sets the value, and the process follows the statewide calendar. This table collects the dates a seller most often needs, as printed by the Texas Comptroller.

Texas property tax dates that affect a Texarkana sale
DateWhat happens
January 1Value is set and the tax lien attaches
April 30Deadline for many exemption applications
May 15Usual last day to protest, or 30 days after the notice, whichever is later
October 1Tax bills go out
January 31Last day to pay without delinquency
February 1Unpaid taxes are delinquent; 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest added

Bowie CAD says an owner whose market value rose by at least $1,000 gets a Notice of Appraised Value each spring, showing market value, assessed value and taxable value. A protest can be mailed to P.O. Box 6527, Texarkana, TX 75505 or dropped off at 122A Plaza West in Texarkana or at 710 James Bowie Drive in New Boston. Informal meetings with an appraiser come first, and the appraisal review board hears unresolved cases.

sections.h2: What exemptions and tax limits matter when selling in Texarkana?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption reduces the taxable value of your main residence, and the buyer will want to know what the house costs to carry. Texas school districts must give a $140,000 residence homestead exemption, with another $60,000 for owners 65 or older and disabled owners.

  • Homestead appraised value can rise no more than 10 percent per year under the state cap.
  • Owners 65 or older and disabled owners get a school tax ceiling that can transfer to a new Texas home.
  • Disabled veterans can qualify for exemptions ranging by rating, and 100 percent disabled veterans can get a total homestead exemption.

If you move out before April 30, ask Bowie CAD how to cancel your exemption so the buyer can apply for theirs. The Comptroller notes a buyer acquiring after January 1 can get the exemption for the rest of the tax year when the prior owner did not hold one.

sections.h2: What should I do about back taxes or a lien before a Texarkana sale?
sections.html:
Pay or payoff the amounts through closing. The Comptroller explains that a lien attaches on January 1 each year and survives a change of ownership, so a buyer cannot get clear title until delinquent taxes are cleared.

Penalties climb on a schedule: 6 percent and 1 percent interest on February 1, then penalty and interest keep growing each month, with the penalty reaching 12 percent on July 1 and an attorney fee of up to 20 percent possible where the taxing unit has a contract. Ask the Bowie County tax office for a payoff figure good through your closing date.

Homestead owners may qualify for an installment plan on delinquent taxes, and some collectors allow up to 36 months. Seniors and disabled homeowners may pay a current bill in four installments. A penalty waiver can be requested in writing but has a short window after you learn of the delinquency.

sections.h2: How do I handle an inherited, foreclosed or occupied Texarkana house?
sections.html:
Texas law gives each a defined path. For an inherited house, a will generally must be probated within four years of death, and a small estate affidavit covers estates up to $75,000 not counting the homestead. A recorded transfer on death deed passes property without probate, and a recorded affidavit of heirship is another option, though third parties are not required to accept it.

For foreclosure, the State Law Library says Texas sales happen at public auction on the first Tuesday of a month after at least 21 days' notice, with the notice posted at the courthouse and filed with the county clerk. A borrower can reinstate by paying what is past due within 20 days of the default notice. Selling first can protect your equity.

For an occupied house, an owner dealing with someone who stayed after being told to leave may be able to use the constable or sheriff removal request under Property Code chapter 24B, but not when the occupant is a family member or a current or former tenant. Tenants need written notice to vacate, at least three days unless the lease says otherwise, followed by a justice court case.

sections.h2: How is the deed recorded and what does it cost?
sections.html:
The Bowie County Clerk records the deed, because Texas deed records are kept in the county where the land sits. The deed must be signed and acknowledged before a notary or other authorized officer to be recorded.

The 2023 clerk manual lists a $5.00 fee for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus records management, archive and technology fees. Ask your title company or the clerk for the current total.

faqs.q: Which state's law applies to my Texarkana house?
faqs.a: The law of the state where the property sits. A house on the Texas side follows Texas rules and is recorded in Bowie County, while a house on the Arkansas side follows Arkansas rules. Check your deed and tax bill to confirm the side.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to protest my Bowie County appraisal?
faqs.a: May 15, or 30 days after the notice is mailed, whichever is later. Bowie CAD accepts protests online, by mail and at its Texarkana and New Boston offices.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Texarkana house if I owe property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid taxes, penalty and interest are paid from the proceeds at closing. Get a payoff figure from the tax office so the closing statement matches.

faqs.q: Do I need to repair my Texarkana house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. Cash buyers commonly buy as is and set the price with repairs in mind. A buyer using a mortgage is more likely to require fixes.

faqs.q: Does the buyer keep my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The exemption belongs to the owner. A buyer who moves in applies for their own, and the Comptroller says they can claim it for the rest of the year if the previous owner did not.
